label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
To: timeline
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: none

Spent the last two Saturdays redoing the electric in a buddy’s shed. And boy, somebody had been creative.

The power started out as three orange extension cords daisy chained out the basement window, across the yard and under the deck. One splice was wrapped in duct tape. Not electrical tape. Duct tape. I guess if it fixes the dryer vent, why not the entire electrical system.

There was a 30 amp breaker feeding 14 gauge wire, an outlet hooked up with speaker wire, and my personal favorite: a regular outlet with a GFCI sticker stuck on it. Fellas, the sticker does not make it a GFCI any more than a Steelers sticker makes my truck a linebacker.

The ceiling fan box was hanging on by one drywall screw. One. There was also a mouse nest in a junction box. Mice were fine, by the way. They looked at me like I was the one who didn’t belong there.

And inside the panel door, written in Sharpie: “SHED - DONT TOUCH - RON.”

My buddy’s wife was standing there when I opened it. She looks at me and says, “Who’s Ron?”

Lady, I have no idea. But apparently Ron had some concerns.

Now, I don’t think whoever did this was evil. Probably just cheap and a little proud, and figured he could make it work. That’s most of these jobs. But making it work for a while and making it safe are two different things.

That oversized breaker and undersized wire is the kind of thing that can let a wire overheat without the breaker protecting it properly. Bad splices and makeshift wiring can start fires. A sticker sure as hell won’t protect anybody from a shock. This stuff really does burn houses down, and somebody can get hurt long before you smell anything.

We got it cleaned up: trenched in a proper line, put it on a 20 amp GFCI breaker, installed real boxes and outlets, and got the fan on a proper brace. Fan runs, nobody’s getting cooked, and the mice will have to find another apartment.

Payment was two pizzas and a case of Yuengling, which I’m pretty sure puts me in a different tax bracket.

Seriously though, if you’ve got a shed, garage or basement wired up with a collection of mystery cords and good intentions, call a licensed electrician. Not your buddy who watched one YouTube video and now owns a roll of tape. I’ve been doing this a long time and I still test everything. There’s no shame in asking somebody who knows.
